To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
depictive secondary predicates may refer not only to direct objects, but also to indirect objects, and more oblique comple-ments.

depictive secondary predicates are not raised from the complement clause, that they can refer to more oblique complemets, that this is more marked, and that the analysis of depictive secondary predicates is parallel to the analysis of control constructions.

depictive secondary predicates are controlled by the underlying syntactic representation of the argument-structure of the main predicate, that depictives are not raising constructions, and that the markedness of reference to oblique complements can be explained by the obliqueness hierachy of Keenan and Comire.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how the syntactic-semantic interface is organized and how this interface can be described in a compositional fashion.
the question how depictive secondary predicates are licensed in German and what the underlying syntactic representation looks like.
the question of how the syntactic and semantic properties of a secondary predicate can be derived from the properties of the underlying argument-structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
depictive secondary predicates are not a special syntactic phenomenon but are rather an instantiation of the general syntactic-semantic phenomenon of control constructions.
depictive secondary predicates are a special type of control construction.
the analysis of depictives in German is a matter of syntactic-semantic interface phenomena, and not a matter of syntactical structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the argument-structure is a more appropriate representation than a surface structure for the analysis of depictive secondary predicates.
the analysis of depictive secondary predicates is based on an HPSG theory of control.
depictive secondary predicates are syntactic elements that can be analyzed in terms of the underlying syntactic structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of depictive secondary predicates should make reference to a representation of the argument-structure that is distinct from the surface representation.
we need to consider the argument-structure when investigating the syntax of depictive secondary predicates.
the analysis of German depictive secondary predicates is not as straightforward as it seems.
